parsed_result.summary: Yes, model family meaningfully affects performance on this dataset: on a held-out test set, GradientBoosting achieved the highest ROC-AUC (0.9290) while KNN was lowest (0.8944), a gap of 0.0347. Repeated cross-validation confirmed this gap is stable and statistically distinguishable from zero, though the two best non-linear models (RandomForest and GradientBoosting) perform similarly to each other.
parsed_result.primary_metric_name: ROC-AUC difference (GradientBoosting - KNN, 5x5 repeated CV mean)
parsed_result.direction: GradientBoosting > KNN (all models: GradientBoosting=0.9278, LogisticRegression=0.9067, RandomForest=0.9031, KNN=0.8953)
parsed_result.methodological_choices: Missing categorical values (workclass, occupation, native-country; ~7% of rows) kept as an explicit 'Missing' category rather than dropped or imputed by mode, since missingness may be informative (e.g. never-worked). Target binarized (>50K=1). Numeric features standardized, categoricals one-hot encoded, same pipeline applied to all model families for a fair/consistent comparison rather than model-specific encodings (e.g. native ordinal/target encoding for trees). Compared 4 model families spanning different inductive biases: Logistic Regression (linear), Random Forest (300 trees), HistGradientBoostingClassifier (boosted trees, default params), and KNN (k=25, chosen to be reasonably robust given ~39k training rows after one-hot expansion to ~100 dims). No SMOTE/class reweighting applied for the ~76/24 class imbalance; ROC-AUC chosen as primary metric specifically because it is threshold-independent and reasonably robust to this level of imbalance (accuracy and F1 also reported for context). Primary split: single stratified 80/20 train/test split, random_state=42.
parsed_result.verification_method: 5x repeated stratified 5-fold cross-validation (25 total folds, different seed from the primary split) on the training portion of the data, comparing mean ROC-AUC per model family. Additionally computed a paired bootstrap (10,000 resamples) 95% CI on the fold-wise AUC gap between the best and worst model family to assess whether the gap is distinguishable from zero, and checked whether the best/worst model ranking from the single held-out split matches the CV ranking.
parsed_result.verification_result: Finding held up. CV ranking matched the held-out split ranking (GradientBoosting best, KNN worst). CV AUC: LogisticRegression=0.9067(sd=0.0033), RandomForest=0.9031(sd=0.0037), GradientBoosting=0.9278(sd=0.0031), KNN=0.8953(sd=0.0032). Paired bootstrap 95% CI on the (GradientBoosting - KNN) gap: [0.0318, 0.0332], which excludes zero, confirming the gap is real and not due to sampling noise.
